meta.description: HUD element reference for building custom script menus in CoD4/CoD4X and MW2/IW4X GSC

positioning.description: How to position HUD elements on screen. The virtual resolution is always 640x480 regardless of the player's actual screen resolution.

virtual_resolution.note: All HUD coordinates are in this virtual space. 320,240 is screen center.

setPoint.description: Primary positioning API. Places the 'align' anchor of the element at offset (x,y) from the 'relative' point on the screen.

parameters.align: Which part of this element is the anchor point.
parameters.relative: Which point on the screen (or parent element) the offset is measured from.
parameters.x: Horizontal offset in virtual pixels. Negative = left.
parameters.y: Vertical offset in virtual pixels. Negative = up.

examples.description: Stack option text below a title element

direct_properties.description: Lower-level alternative to setPoint. Use when setPoint is unavailable or you need fine-grained control.

x.description: Horizontal offset from the horzAlign origin.

y.description: Vertical offset from the vertAlign origin.

horzAlign.description: Screen edge used as the x origin.

vertAlign.description: Screen edge used as the y origin.

top_right_column.description: Start of a right-aligned menu column

bottom_bar.description: Full-width bar at the bottom of the screen

properties.description: All settable properties on HUD elements created with newClientHudElem or createFontString.

newClientHudElem.description: Creates a HUD element visible only to one player. Use for rectangles, shaders, icons. MUST call setParent(level.uiParent) immediately after.
newClientHudElem.note: Called as a free function or on level — NOT on self. Do NOT call setText() on these elements. Use createFontString for text.

createFontString.description: Creates a text HUD element. Called ON the player (self). Use setText() to set content.
createFontString.note: Do NOT call setShader() on text elements created this way.

sort.description: Draw order. Higher values render on top of lower values.
sort.note: Elements with equal sort values have undefined draw order relative to each other.

foreground.description: If true, renders in front of the 3D world. The element is always visible regardless of in-game geometry.

glowColor.description: Text glow color. Only meaningful on text (createFontString) elements.

glowAlpha.description: Text glow intensity. Only meaningful on text elements.

font.note: Only these engine font names work. Any other string silently falls back to default or causes errors.

fontscale.description: Scale multiplier applied to the base font size.

label.description: Localized string reference key (e.g. '@MPUI_KILLS'). Automatically reflects locale changes. Set via elem.label = &"KEY";

width.description: Set implicitly by setShader(material, width, height). NOT directly assignable as elem.width = N.

height.description: Set implicitly by setShader(material, width, height). NOT directly assignable.

setParent.description: MANDATORY for newClientHudElem. Must be called immediately after creation. Without it, elements may not display or may clip incorrectly.

layering.description: How to build layered visual menus with backgrounds, highlights, and text.

shader_rect.description: Creates a solid-color filled rectangle using the engine's built-in blank texture. Color is then set via elem.color.

sort_system.description: Plan your sort layers before creating elements. Elements with higher sort values always render on top.

layer_stack_example.description: Large semi-transparent black rect over full screen
Colored bar showing the selected option
Text labels for each menu option
Menu title (same layer as option text is fine)
Any element that must appear over everything

foreground_note.description: foreground = true renders an element over the 3D world at all times. Useful so your menu stays visible mid-game, but can cause visual artifacts if overused.

cleanup.description: EVERY HUD element created must be explicitly destroyed when the menu closes. Skipping destroy() causes elements to persist and accumulate (visual and memory leak).

cod4_vs_iw4x.description: Key difference in input detection for script menus.
cod4_vs_iw4x.iw4x_mw2: notifyOnPlayerCommand("ev", "+actionslot 1") then self waittill("ev") — pure GSC, no .menu file needed.
cod4_vs_iw4x.cod4_iw3: Requires a compiled .menu file with scriptMenuResponse + waittill("menuresponse", menu, response) in GSC. notifyOnPlayerCommand does NOT exist in stock CoD4.
cod4_vs_iw4x.cod4x: CoD4X (community client) backports notifyOnPlayerCommand from IW4, so IW4X-style pure-GSC menus work there too.
